text:
Predicates:
FinancialAid(x) ::: x is provided financial aid
ProveHardship(x) ::: x proves economic hardship
SingleParent(x) ::: x lives in a single-parent family
FewResources(x) ::: x has few resources available
LivesInSingleParentFamily(x) ::: x lives in a single-parent family
HasFewResources(x) ::: x has few resources available
Applying(x, y) ::: x is applying to y
GRETest(x) ::: x takes the GRE test
Cost(y) ::: y costs money
CheaperThan(y, z) ::: y costs less than z
ProvidesFinancialAid(x, y) ::: x provides financial aid to y

Premises:
Cost(greTest, 205) ::: It costs $205 to take the GRE test.
CheaperThan(205, 300) ::: $205 is cheaper than $300.
ProvidesFinancialAid(ets, y) ← ProveHardship(y) ::: ETS provides financial aid to those who prove hardship.
LivesInSingleParentFamily(tom) ::: Tom lives in a single-parent family.
ProveHardship(tom) ← SingleParent(tom) ∨ FewResources(tom) ::: Tom can prove hardship because he is in a single-parent family or has few resources.
Applying(tom, greTest) ::: Tom is applying to take the GRE test.

Conclusion:
¬∃x (Applying(x, greTest) ∧ FinancialAid(x)) ::: No one taking the GRE test has financial aid provided to them.
